blocks.text: Yeh Unit 4 (Differential Equations) ke poore unit se practice MCQs hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah, jis mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.
4.1 Differential equations: Definition, Order and Degree

blocks.prompt:
1 Which one of the following is a differential equation?
(In mein se kaun si differential equation (tafarruqi muadla) hai?)
blocks.explanation: Differential equation mein kam az kam aik derivative hona zaroori hai. Sirf \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^{2} + y\) mein derivative hai; baqi teen aam equations hain.

book_ref.quote: An equation that involves at least one derivative of a dependent variable with respect to an independent variable is called a differential equation

blocks.prompt:
2 Why is \(y = \sin x + 4\) not a differential equation?
(\(y = \sin x + 4\) differential equation kyun nahi hai?)

options.text: Is mein y ka koi derivative nahi

blocks.explanation: Differential equation mein kam az kam aik derivative hona chahiye. Is mein koi derivative nahi, is liye yeh differential equation nahi (sine ya constant se farq nahi parta).

book_ref.quote: is not a differential equation, because no derivative appears in it

blocks.prompt:
3 In the differential equation \(\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = 5Q\), the dependent variable is:
(Differential equation \(\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = 5Q\) mein dependent variable (taabe variable) kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{dQ}{dt}\) mein jis ka derivative liya ja raha hai, yani \(Q\), dependent variable hai; \(t\) independent variable hai.

book_ref.quote: is the independent variable (we choose it freely)

blocks.prompt:
4 A differential equation is called an ordinary differential equation when:
(Differential equation ko ordinary differential equation kab kehte hain?)

options.text: Is mein sirf first derivatives hon
Is mein sirf aik independent variable ho
Is mein constant term na ho

blocks.explanation: \"Ordinary\" ka matlab sirf aik independent variable, is liye sirf \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) jaise ordinary derivatives aate hain. Iska order ya degree se taalluq nahi.

book_ref.quote: means there is only one independent variable, so only ordinary derivatives

blocks.prompt:
5 If \(v = \dfrac{ds}{dt}\) and \(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt}\), then the acceleration \(a\) in terms of \(s\) is:
(Agar \(v = \dfrac{ds}{dt}\) aur \(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt}\) hon to acceleration \(a\), \(s\) ki soorat mein kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{ds}{dt}\right) = \frac{d^{2}s}{dt^{2}}\), yani \(s\) ka doosra derivative. Pehle derivative ka square alag cheez hai.

book_ref.quote: For example, if a particle covers a distance

blocks.prompt:
6 The order of the differential equation \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 4\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{3} - y = x\) is:
(Differential equation \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 4\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{3} - y = x\) ka order kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Sab se oonchi derivative \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) hai jis ka order 2 hai. Power 3 pehle derivative ki hai, order par asar nahi.

book_ref.quote: The order of a differential equation is the order of the highest derivative that appears in the differential equation.

blocks.prompt:
7 The degree of the differential equation \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 4\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{3} - y = x\) is:
(Differential equation \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 4\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{3} - y = x\) ki degree kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Degree sirf sab se oonche order wali derivative ki power hai. \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ki power 1 hai, is liye degree 1 (cube neeche wali derivative par hai).

book_ref.quote: The degree of a differential equation is the greatest exponent of the highest-order derivative appearing in the differential equation.

blocks.prompt:
8 The order and degree of \(\left(\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\right)^{2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\) are respectively:
(\(\left(\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\right)^{2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\) ka order aur degree tarteeb se kya hain?)
blocks.explanation: Sab se oonchi derivative \(\frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\), is liye order 3. Is ki power 2 hai, is liye degree 2.

book_ref.quote: Look at every derivative in the equation and take the largest such number.

blocks.prompt:
9 The degree of the differential equation \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + e^{dy/dx} = x\) is:
(Differential equation \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + e^{dy/dx} = x\) ki degree kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Derivative \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) exponential ke andar hai, is liye equation derivatives mein polynomial nahi ban sakti; degree define nahi (order 2 hai).

book_ref.quote: If a derivative is stuck inside sin, cos, log, an exponential, etc., the degree is not defined

blocks.prompt:
10 The degree of \(\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2}} = \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) is:
(\(\sqrt{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2}} = \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ki degree kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Dono taraf square karein: \(1 + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} = \left(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right)^{2}\). Ab sab se oonchi derivative ki power 2 hai, is liye degree 2.

book_ref.quote: First clear any root or fractional power that contains a derivative

blocks.prompt:
11 The degree of \(3\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{4} - xy = 0\) is:
(\(3\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{4} - xy = 0\) ki degree kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Sab se oonchi derivative \(\frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\) hai, power 1, is liye degree 1. Power 4 neeche wali derivative par hai.

book_ref.quote: Taking the largest power anywhere as the degree

blocks.prompt:
12 Which one of the following is a first-order differential equation?
(In mein se kaun si first-order differential equation hai?)
blocks.explanation: Order 1 ka matlab sab se oonchi derivative \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ho. Sirf pehli equation mein doosri ya teesri derivative nahi (degree 2 hai magar order 1).

book_ref.quote: A differential equation of order 1 is called a first-order differential equation

blocks.prompt:
13 The order and degree of \(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \left(x + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{1/2}\) are respectively:
(\(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \left(x + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{1/2}\) ka order aur degree tarteeb se kya hain?)
blocks.explanation: Root hatane ke liye square karein: \(\left(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right)^{2} = x + \frac{dy}{dx}\). Sab se oonchi derivative ka order 2, power 2: order 2, degree 2.

book_ref.quote: First-order differential equations (order 1) are the subject of this unit.

blocks.text: 4.1.1 Construction of First-Order and Differential Equations from Practical Situations

blocks.prompt:
14 A quantity \(Q\) changes at a rate proportional to \(Q\) itself. The differential equation is:
(Aik quantity \(Q\) is raftaar se badalti hai jo khud \(Q\) ke proportional (mutanasib) hai. Differential equation kya hogi?)
blocks.explanation: \"\(Q\) ki rate of change\" \(\frac{dQ}{dt}\) hai, aur \"\(Q\) ke proportional\" ka matlab \"\(= k \times Q\)\". Is liye \(\frac{dQ}{dt} = kQ\).

book_ref.quote: First-order differential equations model problems where the rate of change of a quantity depends on the quantity itself or on time.

blocks.prompt:
15 A medicine is removed from the blood at a rate proportional to the amount \(A\) present. With \(k > 0\), the model is:
(Dawai khoon se is raftaar se nikalti hai jo maujood miqdaar \(A\) ke proportional hai. \(k > 0\) ke saath model kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Miqdaar kam ho rahi hai, is liye rate negative hai: \(\frac{dA}{dt} = -kA\), \(k > 0\).

book_ref.quote: Decide the sign: if the quantity is decreasing, its rate is negative

blocks.prompt:
16 The volume \(V\) of water in a leaking tank decreases at a rate proportional to \(\sqrt{V}\). With \(k > 0\), the differential equation is:
(Leak karti tanki mein paani ka volume \(V\) is raftaar se kam hota hai jo \(\sqrt{V}\) ke proportional hai. \(k > 0\) ke saath differential equation kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Rate of change \(\frac{dV}{dt}\); \(\sqrt{V}\) ke proportional se \(k\sqrt{V}\); kam ho raha hai is liye minus: \(\frac{dV}{dt} = -k\sqrt{V}\).

book_ref.quote: from a situation is a translation job

blocks.prompt:
17 In the model \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\) for a population, the population remains constant when:
(Population ke model \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\) mein population kab constant (yaksaan) rehti hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(k = 0\) ho to \(\frac{dP}{dt} = 0\), is liye \(P\) nahi badalti. \(k > 0\) se growth aur \(k < 0\) se decay.

book_ref.quote: The rate of change of a population is proportional to the population itself.

blocks.prompt:
18 In the price model \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\) (\(P > 0\)), deflation corresponds to:
(Qeemat ke model \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\) (\(P > 0\)) mein deflation (qeematon ka girna) kis soorat mein hai?)
blocks.explanation: Deflation ka matlab qeemat kam ho rahi hai, \(\frac{dP}{dt} < 0\). \(P > 0\) ke saath is ke liye \(k < 0\) chahiye.

book_ref.quote: Inflation means the price of goods is increasing over time, while deflation means the price of goods is decreasing over time.

blocks.prompt:
19 With \(k > 0\), Newton's law of cooling or heating for a body at temperature \(T\) in surroundings at constant temperature \(T_{S}\) is:
(\(k > 0\) ke saath, \(T_{S}\) constant temperature wale mahol mein \(T\) temperature wali cheez ke liye Newton's law of cooling ya heating kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Rate farq ke proportional hai, aur \(k > 0\) ke saath bracket \(T_{S} - T\) hona chahiye taa ke garam cheez thandi ho. \(k(T - T_{S})\) se garam cheez aur garam hogi.

book_ref.quote: the rate of change of the body's temperature with respect to time is proportional to the difference between the body's temperature and the surrounding temperature

blocks.prompt:
20 In \(\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\) with \(k > 0\), if \(T > T_{S}\) then:
(\(\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\), \(k > 0\) mein agar \(T > T_{S}\) ho to:)
blocks.explanation: \(T_{S} - T < 0\) aur \(k > 0\), is liye \(\frac{dT}{dt} < 0\): cheez thandi ho rahi hai.

book_ref.quote: the body is cooling down and

blocks.prompt:
21 A pie at \(70^{\circ}\)C is in a room at \(20^{\circ}\)C, and \(\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\) with \(k = 0.1\) per minute. At that moment \(\dfrac{dT}{dt}\) is:
(\(70^{\circ}\)C ki pie \(20^{\circ}\)C ke kamre mein hai, \(\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\), \(k = 0.1\) per minute. Us lamhe \(\dfrac{dT}{dt}\) kitna hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{dT}{dt} = 0.1(20 - 70) = -5\) degree per minute; negative, yani pie thandi ho rahi hai.

book_ref.quote: so the tea cools, exactly as in real life

blocks.prompt:
22 In an RC circuit, the voltage across a capacitor of capacitance \(C\) carrying charge \(q\) is:
(RC circuit mein \(C\) capacitance wale capacitor par charge \(q\) ho to us ke across voltage kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Capacitor ka voltage = charge taqseem capacitance: \(V_{C} = \frac{q}{C}\).

book_ref.quote: The voltage across the capacitor is

blocks.prompt:
23 In the RC circuit model, the current \(I\) and the charge \(q\) are related by:
(RC circuit model mein current \(I\) aur charge \(q\) ka taalluq kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Current charge ke bahao ki raftaar hai, \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\). Is se circuit ka qanoon \(q\) mein differential equation ban jata hai.

book_ref.quote: current is the rate of flow of charge

blocks.prompt:
24 For a resistor \(R\) and capacitor \(C\) in series with a source of emf \(V_{S}\), Kirchhoff's voltage law gives:
(Resistor \(R\) aur capacitor \(C\) series mein, emf \(V_{S}\) ke saath. Kirchhoff's voltage law se kya milta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(V_{S} = V_{R} + V_{C} = IR + \frac{q}{C}\) aur \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\), is liye \(R\frac{dq}{dt} + \frac{q}{C} = V_{S}\).

book_ref.quote: By Kirchhoff's voltage law, the sum of the voltages across the resistor and capacitor equals the total voltage from the battery

blocks.prompt:
25 The voltage across an inductor of inductance \(L\) carrying current \(I\) is:
(\(L\) inductance wale inductor mein current \(I\) ho to us ke across voltage kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Inductor ka voltage current ke badalne ki raftaar ke proportional hai: \(V_{L} = L\frac{dI}{dt}\). (\(RI\) resistor ka voltage hai.)

book_ref.quote: an inductor opposes a change of current; its voltage is proportional to how fast the current changes

blocks.prompt:
26 The RL circuit model \(L\dfrac{dI}{dt} + RI = V_{S}\) can be written as:
(RL circuit model \(L\dfrac{dI}{dt} + RI = V_{S}\) ko kis tarah likh sakte hain?)
blocks.explanation: \(RI\) ko doosri taraf le jayein: \(L\frac{dI}{dt} = V_{S} - RI\); \(L\) se taqseem: \(\frac{dI}{dt} = \frac{V_{S} - RI}{L}\).

book_ref.quote: The sum of the voltages across the resistor and inductor equals the applied voltage

blocks.prompt:
27 For the model \(RC\dfrac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S} - q\), the order and degree are respectively:
(Model \(RC\dfrac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S} - q\) ka order aur degree tarteeb se kya hain?)
blocks.explanation: Sirf pehla derivative \(\frac{dq}{dt}\) hai, power 1: order 1, degree 1.

book_ref.quote: All these are first-order, first-degree differential equations.

blocks.text: 4.2 Solution of First-Order and First-Degree Differential Equations

blocks.prompt:
28 The general form of a first-order, first-degree differential equation is:
(First-order, first-degree differential equation ki general (aam) shakal kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: First order: sirf \(\frac{dy}{dx}\); first degree: power 1. Is liye equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) ki shakal mein likhi ja sakti hai.

book_ref.quote: General form of the first order and first degree differential equations.

blocks.prompt:
29 If \(M(x, y)\,dx + N(x, y)\,dy = 0\) with \(N \ne 0\), then \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) equals:
(Agar \(M(x, y)\,dx + N(x, y)\,dy = 0\) aur \(N \ne 0\), to \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(N\,dy = -M\,dx\), is liye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{M}{N}\).

book_ref.quote: It is always possible to write the above equation in differential form as follows:

blocks.prompt:
30 In differential form, \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x - y}{x + 3y}\) is:
(Differential form mein \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x - y}{x + 3y}\) kya banti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Cross-multiply: \((x + 3y)\,dy = (2x - y)\,dx\). Sab terms aik taraf: \((2x - y)\,dx - (x + 3y)\,dy = 0\); dosri taraf jaane wali term ka sign badalta hai.

book_ref.quote: where \(M(x, y)\) and \(N(x, y)\) are the functions of \(x\) and \(y\).

blocks.prompt:
31 A differential equation together with a condition \(y(x_{0}) = y_{0}\) is called:
(Differential equation aur sharat \(y(x_{0}) = y_{0}\) dono mil kar kya kehlate hain?)
blocks.explanation: Differential equation aur initial value condition \(y(x_{0}) = y_{0}\) mil kar Initial Value Problem (IVP) kehlate hain.

book_ref.quote: A differential equation together with an initial value condition is called an Initial Value Problem (IVP).

blocks.prompt:
32 The initial value condition \(y(2) = 5\) means:
(Initial value condition \(y(2) = 5\) ka matlab kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(y(x_{0}) = y_{0}\) ka matlab \(x = x_{0}\) par \(y = y_{0}\). Is liye \(y(2) = 5\) yani \(x = 2\) par \(y = 5\); yeh zarb nahi.

book_ref.quote: is called an initial value condition or one point boundary condition.

blocks.prompt:
33 The general solution of a first-order differential equation contains:
(First-order differential equation ke general solution mein kya hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: First-order equation ke general solution mein aik arbitrary constant (ikhtiyari constant) hota hai; har qeemat se family ka aik curve milta hai.

book_ref.quote: The general solution contains one arbitrary constant; it is a family of curves.

blocks.prompt:
34 The solution of the IVP \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^{2}\), \(y(1) = 4\) is:
(IVP \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^{2}\), \(y(1) = 4\) ka solution kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: General solution \(y = x^{3} + c\). \(x = 1\), \(y = 4\) rakhein: \(4 = 1 + c\), \(c = 3\), is liye \(y = x^{3} + 3\).

book_ref.quote: In an IVP, first find the general solution, then substitute

blocks.prompt:
35 Which function is a solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2y\)?
(Kaun sa function \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2y\) ka solution hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(y = 5e^{2x}\) ke liye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 10e^{2x} = 2y\), identity ban jati hai. Baqi fail hote hain, maslan \(y = 2e^{x}\) se \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2e^{x} \ne 4e^{x}\).

book_ref.quote: A solution of a differential equation is a function defined on some interval

blocks.prompt:
36 Which one of the following differential equations is separable?
(In mein se kaun si differential equation separable hai?)

book_ref.quote: A first-order, first-degree differential equation is called Separable if it can be written as:

blocks.prompt:
37 Separating the variables in \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{3x + 2y}\) gives:
(\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{3x + 2y}\) mein variables alag karne se kya milta hai?)

book_ref.quote: is not separable: it is, since

blocks.prompt:
38 The general solution of \(y\,dy = x^{2}\,dx\) is:
(\(y\,dy = x^{2}\,dx\) ka general solution kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: By solving the integrals on both sides, we obtain the general solution of separable differential equation.

blocks.prompt:
39 The general solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2xy\) is (\(A\) an arbitrary constant):
(\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2xy\) ka general solution kya hai (\(A\) arbitrary constant)?)

book_ref.quote: Add one arbitrary constant (on one side only) and simplify.

blocks.prompt:
40 The general solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin y}\) is:
(\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin y}\) ka general solution kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin y\,dy = \cos x\,dx\), is liye \(-\cos y = \sin x + c_{1}\), yani \(\sin x + \cos y = c\).

book_ref.quote: We can separate the variables: put everything with

blocks.prompt:
41 The general solution of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + y^{2}\) is:
(\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + y^{2}\) ka general solution kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{dy}{1 + y^{2}} = dx\), aur \(\int\frac{dy}{1 + y^{2}} = \tan^{-1}y\). Is liye \(\tan^{-1}y = x + c\).

book_ref.quote: Method: separate, integrate both sides, add one constant.

blocks.prompt:
42 After integrating both sides of a separable equation we may get \(+c_{1}\) on the left and \(+c_{2}\) on the right. We write only one constant because:
(Separable equation ke dono taraf integrate karne se baen \(+c_{1}\) aur daen \(+c_{2}\) aata hai. Hum sirf aik constant kyun likhte hain?)

options.text: dono mil kar aik constant \(c = c_{2} - c_{1}\) bante hain
baen taraf integration ka constant nahi aata

blocks.explanation: \(c_{1}\) ko daen taraf le jaane se \(c_{2} - c_{1}\) banta hai, jo phir bhi sirf aik arbitrary constant \(c\) hai.

book_ref.quote: moving them together gives a single constant

blocks.prompt:
43 Besides its general solution, the equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x(y - 2)\) has the constant solution:
(General solution ke ilawa \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x(y - 2)\) ka constant solution kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yahan \(h(y) = y - 2\), \(y = 2\) par zero hai. \(y = 2\) ke liye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 0 = x(2 - 2)\), is liye \(y = 2\) solution hai.

book_ref.quote: Small caution: dividing by

blocks.prompt:
44 The family \(x^{2} + 4y^{2} = c\) is the general solution of:
(Family \(x^{2} + 4y^{2} = c\) kis equation ka general solution hai?)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate karein: \(2x + 8y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\), is liye \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x}{4y}\).

book_ref.quote: Check by differentiating the answer: you must get the original equation back.

blocks.prompt:
45 The solution of the IVP \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{y}\), \(y(0) = 2\) is:
(IVP \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{y}\), \(y(0) = 2\) ka solution kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: Separable means \(\frac{dy}{dx} = g(x)\,h(y)\)

blocks.prompt:
46 The solution of the IVP \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\) (\(x > 0\)), \(y(1) = 3\) is:
(IVP \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\) (\(x > 0\)), \(y(1) = 3\) ka solution kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{dy}{y} = \frac{dx}{x}\) se \(\ln|y| = \ln|x| + \ln|c|\), yani \(y = cx\). Phir \(3 = c\): \(y = 3x\).

book_ref.quote: Integrating a side that still contains both

blocks.prompt:
47 Which one of the following differential equations is homogeneous?
(In mein se kaun si differential equation homogeneous hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x^{2} + y^{2}\) aur \(xy\) ki har term ki degree 2 hai; \(x^{2}\) se taqseem par \(\frac{1 + (y/x)^{2}}{y/x} = F\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\). Baqi teen mein degrees mili juli hain.

book_ref.quote: A first-order, first degree differential equation is called Homogeneous if it can be written in the form

blocks.prompt:
48 To solve a homogeneous differential equation, the substitution used is:
(Homogeneous differential equation hal karne ke liye kaun si substitution (badal) istemal hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(y = vx\) rakhein, \(v\), \(x\) ka function hai; product rule se \(\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}\). Sirf \(v\) likhna doosri term bhool jana hai.

book_ref.quote: can be converted into a separable differential equation in variables

blocks.prompt:
49 With \(y = vx\), the right side of \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^{3} + y^{3}}{x^{2}y}\) becomes:
(\(y = vx\) rakhne se \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^{3} + y^{3}}{x^{2}y}\) ka daayan hissa kya banta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x\) ki jagah 1 aur \(y\) ki jagah \(v\): \(\frac{1 + v^{3}}{v}\). (Seedha: \(\frac{x^{3}(1 + v^{3})}{x^{3}v}\).)

book_ref.quote: can easily be simplified by replacing

blocks.prompt:
50 For \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\), after putting \(y = vx\) the separable form is:
(\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)\) mein \(y = vx\) rakhne ke baad separable shakal kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(v + x\frac{dv}{dx} = F(v)\), is liye \(x\frac{dv}{dx} = F(v) - v\) aur \(\frac{dv}{F(v) - v} = \frac{dx}{x}\). \(v\) tafreeq karna bhoolna aam ghalti hai.

book_ref.quote: It becomes separable differential equation.

blocks.prompt:
51 Which right side \(f(x, y)\) satisfies \(f(tx, ty) = f(x, y)\), so that \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) is homogeneous?
(Kaun sa \(f(x, y)\) \(f(tx, ty) = f(x, y)\) poora karta hai, taa ke \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\) homogeneous ho?)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{t^{2}x^{2} - t^{2}y^{2}}{t^{2}xy} = \frac{x^{2} - y^{2}}{xy}\): koi tabdeeli nahi. Baqi badal jate hain.

book_ref.quote: A homogeneous right side must not change when

blocks.prompt:
52 Putting \(y = vx\) in \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - y}{x + y}\) gives \(x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\) equal to:
(\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - y}{x + y}\) mein \(y = vx\) rakhne se \(x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\) kya banta hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(v + x\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{1 - v}{1 + v}\), is liye \(x\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{1 - v - v(1 + v)}{1 + v} = \frac{1 - 2v - v^{2}}{1 + v}\).
